Simplified Approach for Braced Wall Panel Length

Gypsum-Sheathed Framing Type (with gypsum board on only

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
This Article applies to buildings where
(a) the seismic design parameter, Smax, is not greater than 0.47,
(b) the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than
0.60 kPa, (c) the specified roof snow load, as calculated in
accordance with Article 9.4.2.2, is not greater than 2 kPa, (d) the
plan dimensions of the building are each not greater than 21.2 m,
(e) the building is located in rough terrain, as described in Note
A-9.23.13.7.(3) and (4), (f) the greatest eave-to-ridge height of
the roof is not greater than 3 m, (g) the braced wall panels are
constructed with gypsum board on at least one side, (h) the braced
wall bands are continuously sheathed, and (i) the building is of
normal-weight construction, as defined in Clause 9.23.13.2.(3)(a),
except as provided in Sentence (4).
Except as provided in Sentence (3), the minimum total length
of all braced wall panels in each direction is determined in
accordance with
(a) Table 9.23.13.11-A where Smax is not greater than 0.3 and HWP
is not greater than 0.5 kPa, or (b) Table 9.23.13.11-B.
Except as provided in Sentence (4), the minimum total length
of all braced wall panels in each braced wall band in the
direction perpendicular to a single building face partially
clad with masonry veneer is determined in accordance with
(a) Table 9.23.13.11-C where Smax is not greater than 0.3 and HWP
is not greater than 0.50 kPa, or (b) Table 9.23.13.11-D
Wall portions clad with masonry veneer that are located both
perpendicular to a braced wall band and within a braced wall
band are permitted to be considered as normal-weight
construction.
Bracing to resist lateral loads is designed and constructed in
accordance with Articles A-9.23.13.4. to 9.23.13.6 and
Tables as printed, storey icons redrawn. In Tables -A and -B the row 2 icons repeat row 1, as printed. Also as printed: “Masonary”.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.13.11. (page 9-214)
